headline: Ukraine Says Attacks Caused Emergency Outages in Kyiv and Five Regions
deck: Ukraine's Energy Ministry said attacks damaged facilities in Kyiv and five regions, triggering emergency power outages.
body: Ukraine’s Energy Ministry said Russian attacks damaged energy facilities in Kyiv and five regions on 16 October. [E2]
A Reuters title said more than one million consumers had faced power cuts at some point. [E1]
On 13 October, this paper reported that Russia had hit no Ukrainian energy targets for a day. [E10]
The ministry listed Kyiv, the Kyiv, Kharkiv, Rivne, Volyn and Odesa regions, and said damage from the strikes triggered emergency power outages. [E4]
It said Russian forces had struck energy facilities in waves of drone attacks from early morning through the day. [E3]
Associated Press reported that attacks across nine Ukrainian regions knocked out power to hundreds of thousands of households and wounded at least 15 people. [E5]
Russia’s military chief told President Vladimir Putin that the military had allocated assets for its aerial campaign against Ukraine’s energy system, AP reported. [E6]

AP reported that President Donald Trump told Newsmax he disliked dealing with Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy. At an EU summit, Zelenskyy said Ukraine had to prepare for winter because he saw no indication that Russia was ready to end the war. [E7]
AP reported that Ukraine is short of Patriot missiles and that Zelenskyy said higher Starshield speeds needed against jet-powered drones were being restored. [E8]

Putin instructed the military to continue its aerial campaign, while Chief of the General Staff Gen. Valery Gerasimov said strikes on energy facilities, bridges, railways and data centers would continue. [E9]

evidence_box.fragment: Meanwhile, Russia’s military chief reported to President Vladimir Putin on Friday that the military has allocated the necessary assets to press its aerial campaign against Ukraine’s energy system. Russia’s heavy bombardment of the power grid before cold weather arrives has been an annual feature of the war, aiming to wear down Ukraine’s appetite for the fight by denying civilians heat and running water. Ukrainian officials have warned that Russia is stockpiling ballistic missiles for more attacks in the coming months. Ukraine on Thursday abandoned a brief truce on energy-related targets that it said Moscow didn’t heed despite U.S. President Donald Trump’s demand for a ceasefire. The Kremlin said terms of an energy truce had not been set.

evidence_box.fragment: Ukraine is desperately short of the U.S.-made Patriot missiles it needs to protect against Russia’s devastating ballistic missile attacks, despite pleas from Zelenskyy for Washington to send more. He said in Brussels that small numbers of Patriot interceptors have reached Ukraine in recent months, either bought for Kyiv from the U.S. by European countries or provided by other countries around the world from their own stocks. Zelenskyy complained about a breakdown in Western intelligence sharing and sudden speed restrictions on the use of Starshield, the military-grade version of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service that is the backbone of Ukraine’s drone operations and military communications. The Starshield limits that slowed Ukrainian drone interceptors to 70 kph (43 mph) were “a dangerous and unpleasant surprise,” Zelenskyy said in Brussels. But the higher speeds needed to stop jet-powered Russian drones moving at more than 400 kph (250 mph) are being restored, he said.

evidence_box.fragment: Speaking Friday during a visit to military headquarters overseeing operations in Ukraine, Putin hailed Moscow’s gains, emphasizing that capturing the Ukrainian-controlled part of the Donetsk region remains a priority. He also instructed the military to press on with its aerial campaign. Chief of the General Staff, Gen. Valery Gerasimov, reported that the military has launched a series of strikes on Ukraine’s energy facilities and has the means to knock them out. He also said attacks on Ukrainian bridges, railways and data centers will continue.
